title: Introduction to recycle
text: recycle package provides intelligent caching function results comparing function arguments. Unlike simple memoization, recycle offers flexible per-argument comparison logic handles complex scenarios.

title: Introduction to recycle
text: simplest use case caching expensive computation:
code: # Define an expensive function expensive_computation <- function(x, y) {   Sys.sleep(2)  # Simulate expensive operation   x^2 + y^2 }  # First call - executes the function (takes 2 seconds) result1 <- recycle(   expensive_computation,   args = list(x = 3, y = 4),   path.res = "cache/result.rds" ) print(result1)  # 25  # Second call with same arguments - uses cache (instant!) result2 <- recycle(   expensive_computation,   args = list(x = 3, y = 4),   path.res = "cache/result.rds" ) print(result2)  # 25  # Different arguments - re-runs the function result3 <- recycle(   expensive_computation,   args = list(x = 5, y = 12),   path.res = "cache/result.rds" ) print(result3)  # 169

title: Introduction to recycle
text: One recycle’s key features intelligent handling function arguments. pass function argument, recycle automatically compares code (body formals) rather environment.

title: Introduction to recycle
code: # Function that takes another function as argument apply_operation <- function(data, operation) {   operation(data) }  # First call transform1 <- function(x) x * 2 result1 <- recycle(   apply_operation,   args = list(data = 1:10, operation = transform1),   path.res = "cache/transformed.rds" )  # Second call with identical function code - uses cache! transform2 <- function(x) x * 2  # Same code, different object result2 <- recycle(   apply_operation,   args = list(data = 1:10, operation = transform2),   path.res = "cache/transformed.rds" )  # Different function code - re-runs transform3 <- function(x) x * 3 result3 <- recycle(   apply_operation,   args = list(data = 1:10, operation = transform3),   path.res = "cache/transformed.rds" )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: can also explicitly specify function unwrapping using "function" keyword:
code: result <- recycle(   apply_operation,   args = list(data = 1:10, operation = my_fun),   path.res = "cache/result.rds",   args.unwrap = list(operation = "function") )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: common use case processing data files. want re-run analysis file contents change, just file path changes.
code: # Create a sample data file write.csv(mtcars[1:10, ], "data.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # Function that processes a file process_file <- function(file_path, multiplier) {   data <- read.csv(file_path)   data$mpg <- data$mpg * multiplier   return(data) }  # First run - processes the file result1 <- recycle(   process_file,   args = list(file_path = "data.csv", multiplier = 2),   path.res = "cache/processed.rds",   args.unwrap = list(     file_path = function(x) readLines(x, warn = FALSE)   ) )  # Same file, same arguments - uses cache result2 <- recycle(   process_file,   args = list(file_path = "data.csv", multiplier = 2),   path.res = "cache/processed.rds",   args.unwrap = list(     file_path = function(x) readLines(x, warn = FALSE)   ) )  # Modify the file write.csv(mtcars[1:20, ], "data.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # Now it re-runs because file contents changed result3 <- recycle(   process_file,   args = list(file_path = "data.csv", multiplier = 2),   path.res = "cache/processed.rds",   args.unwrap = list(     file_path = function(x) readLines(x, warn = FALSE)   ) )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: Sometimes function saves results custom format (e.g., fst, parquet, feather). recycle supports fun.read save.res parameters.
code: # Example with CSV format save_as_csv <- function(data, output_path) {   write.csv(data, output_path, row.names = FALSE)   return(data) }  result <- recycle(   save_as_csv,   args = list(data = mtcars, output_path = "cache/data.csv"),   path.res = "cache/data.csv",   fun.read = function(path) read.csv(path),  # Custom read function   save.res = FALSE  # Function saves its own results )  # On subsequent calls, uses the custom read function result2 <- recycle(   save_as_csv,   args = list(data = mtcars, output_path = "cache/data.csv"),   path.res = "cache/data.csv",   fun.read = function(path) read.csv(path),   save.res = FALSE )

title: Introduction to recycle
code: library(fst)  save_as_fst <- function(data, output_path) {   write_fst(data, output_path)   return(data) }  result <- recycle(   save_as_fst,   args = list(data = large_dataset, output_path = "cache/data.fst"),   path.res = "cache/data.fst",   fun.read = read_fst,   save.res = FALSE )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: ’s realistic example combining multiple features: example: - transform_fun automatically compared code (auto-detected) - input_file compared contents (custom unwrap function) - config_file compared parsed JSON contents (custom unwrap function) - threshold compared -(numeric value)
code: # Complex analysis function analyze_data <- function(input_file, transform_fun, config_file, threshold) {   # Read data   data <- read.csv(input_file)      # Apply transformation   data$value <- transform_fun(data$value)      # Read configuration   config <- jsonlite::read_json(config_file)      # Filter based on threshold   data <- data[data$value > threshold, ]      return(data) }  # Define transformation function my_transform <- function(x) log(x + 1)  # Run with recycle result <- recycle(   analyze_data,   args = list(     input_file = "data.csv",     transform_fun = my_transform,     config_file = "config.json",     threshold = 5   ),   path.res = "cache/analysis.rds",   args.unwrap = list(     # transform_fun automatically detected as function     input_file = function(x) readLines(x, warn = FALSE),     config_file = function(x) jsonlite::read_json(x)     # threshold compared as-is (numeric value)   ) )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: Sometimes want force re-run regardless whether arguments changed:
code: result <- recycle(   my_function,   args = list(x = 1, y = 2),   path.res = "cache/result.rds",   force = TRUE  # Always re-run )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: default, digests stored alongside results _digests appended filename. can customize :
code: result <- recycle(   my_function,   args = list(x = 1, y = 2),   path.res = "cache/result.rds",   path.digest = "cache/my_custom_digests.rds" )

title: Introduction to recycle
text: Use descriptive cache paths: Organize cache files dedicated directory explicit file unwrapping: Always specify read file contents Consider cache invalidation: Use force = TRUE need ensure fresh results Clean old caches: Periodically remove outdated cache files Use version control wisely: Add cache directories .gitignore
code: path.res = "cache/analysis/step1_results.rds" args.unwrap = list(data_file = readLines) unlink("cache", recursive = TRUE)

title: Smart Function Result Caching with Custom Argument Comparison
text: pass functions arguments, recycle automatically compares code (body formals) rather environment. means two functions identical code different environments treated equivalent.
code: apply_transform <- function(data, transform_fun) {   transform_fun(data) }  # These two calls use the same cached result because the functions are identical transform1 <- function(x) x * 2 result1 <- recycle(apply_transform,                     list(data = mtcars, transform_fun = transform1),                    path.res = "cache/transformed.rds")  transform2 <- function(x) x * 2  # Same code, different object result2 <- recycle(apply_transform,                    list(data = mtcars, transform_fun = transform2),                    path.res = "cache/transformed.rds")  # Uses cache!

title: Smart Function Result Caching with Custom Argument Comparison
text: Compare file contents instead file paths, changes files trigger re-computation:
code: process_data <- function(input_file, param) {   data <- read.csv(input_file)   # ... expensive processing   return(processed_data) }  result <- recycle(   process_data,   args = list(input_file = "data.csv", param = 10),   path.res = "cache/processed.rds",   args.unwrap = list(input_file = function(x) readLines(x, warn = FALSE)) )  # If data.csv changes, the function will re-run automatically

title: Smart caching of function results with custom argument comparison — recycle
text: fun Function execute (retrieve cached results ) args Named list arguments pass `fun` path.res Path file results stored (RDS format) path.digest Path file argument digests stored (RDS format). NULL, defaults `path.res` "_digests" appended extension. args.unwrap Named list specifying unwrap/transform arguments computing digests. Values can : - string "function" compare functions code (ignoring environments) - function apply argument value digesting - NULL arguments compared -Examples: list(myfun = "function", myfile = readLines, x = NULL) fun.read Function read cached results. NULL (default), uses `readRDS(path.res)`. Use `fun` saves results custom format (e.g., fst, parquet, csv). function take one argument: file path. save.res Logical. TRUE (default), `recycle()` saves result using `saveRDS()`. Set FALSE `fun` saves results `path.res`. force Logical. TRUE, always re-run function regardless cached results. Default FALSE. quiet Logical. FALSE (default), prints messages cache status changed. TRUE, runs silently.
